answer: Agents trading tundra weather feeds, quartz assays, or sparrow telemetry can deter Sybil attacks with time-locked collateral bonds. Each agent escrows tokens tied to its public key for an epoch, while challengers submit fraud proofs of double-signing or false claims to trigger slashing. Faking identities forces an attacker to lock scarce liquid capital per account and risk confiscation. Still, wealthy adversaries can fund multiple bonds, skewing influence toward high-capital operators.
